learning_outcomes.text: Students will be introduced to the application of conservation laws and force balance under steady and unsteady fluid flow.
They will apply the obtained knowledge of general mechanics while learning about the continuum mechanics principles.
They will conduct simple experiments to understand the theory.

Having obtained the fundamental knowledge, they will be able to solve practical fluid flow mechanics problems, pressures and pressure forces under steady and unsteady flow in particular, and they will be introduced to more complex engineering problems solutions.

syllabus_topics: Basic concepts of fluid mechanics, physical properties of liquids
Pressure and pressure forces, the liquid at rest, Euler's equation of hydrostatics, constant pressure levels, Pascal's law
Pressure force acting on flat and curved submerged surfaces, Archimedes law, fluids in moving container
Introduction to fluid flow, continuity equation and Bernoulli's equation for ideal fluid flow
Application of Bernoulli's equation for the flow of an ideal fluid, measurement of pressure and flow in pipes
Real fluid flow, Navier-Stokes equation, Bernoulli's equation for an incompressible viscous fluid in a gravity field, Bernoulli's equation for a compressible fluid
Steady flow in pipes, laminar and turbulent flow in pipes of circular cross section
Hydraulic resistances by friction and local loss, hydraulic calculation of pipelines, characteristics of pipelines
Bernoulli equation for the rotating channel, centrifugal pump, pump characteristic curves, pump in the piping system
Liquid outflow from a small orifice, emptying of containers, the liquid discharge through large rectangular hole in the side wall of the container
Unsteady flow of incompressible and compressible liquid through a pipe, hydraulic shock
Theorem about change of momentum and its application
Force effects of flowing fluid on surfaces and bodies, flow around submerged bodies
Physical properties of fluids
Hydrostatic pressure, pressure levels, Pascal's law, pressure force on plane surfaces
Pressure force on curved surfaces, liquid in moving container
Control test No. 1 - Hydrostatics
Continuity equation, Bernoulli's equation for an ideal liquid, measurement of pressure and velocities in pipelines
Bernoulli's equation for a real liquid, specific energy loss, Reynolds number
Hydraulic frictional resistances in laminar and turbulent flow, local resistances
Laboratory measurements (friction and local losses, pump curve)
Hydraulic calculations of pipelines
Bernoulli's equation for a rotating channel, a centrifugal pump, a pump and a pipe
Control test no. 2 - Hydrodynamics
Unsteady flow of incompressible and compressible liquid through pipes, hydraulic shock
Application of the theorem on change of momentum, flow around bodies
